summary:
Illinois is placed in the fifteen-state "Most Protective" tier of a July 2026 national legal-risk ranking compiled from a rubric over thousands of tracked anti-trans bills, which describes the tier's laws as having gone above and beyond in safeguarding trans rights.

Discrimination on the basis of gender identity has been banned in employment, housing, credit and public accommodations since 1 June 2006, with "sexual orientation" defined to include gender-related identity whether or not traditionally associated with the sex assigned at birth. The exemption for employers with fewer than 15 employees was removed by legislation signed in August 2019 and effective 1 July 2020, following a 2018 veto, and discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation in jury selection was banned effective 1 January 2020.

Hate-crime penalties were extended to gender identity by HB 3930, passed unanimously on 16 April and 20 May 2015, signed by Governor Bruce Rauner on 20 July 2015 and effective 1 January 2016; before that, such offences were covered only as perceived sexual orientation. The state's hate-crime statute has provided enhanced penalties for crimes motivated by actual or perceived sexual orientation since 1991. The gay and trans panic defence was repealed by SB1761, passed unanimously in June 2017, signed on 25 August 2017 and effective 1 January 2018.

Gender-affirming care is protected by legislation signed on 13 January 2023 and effective immediately, covering care provided within Illinois, including for people who travel from outside the state to obtain it. Under the shield law, patients and providers are protected from civil or criminal charges where care lawful in Illinois was banned in the patient's home state. Conversion therapy on minors under 18 by mental health providers has been banned under the Youth Mental Health Protection Act since 1 January 2016; a federal court dismissed a challenge brought by pastors on 15 February 2017, holding that private religious counselling is not trade or commerce.

Birth-certificate gender-marker changes no longer require surgery, under legislation passed on 31 May 2017 by 63-43 in the House and 32-22 in the Senate, signed on 25 August 2017 and effective 1 January 2018. An X option has been available since July 2020, and a self-attestation reform passed in January and February 2023 took effect on 1 July. Since 1 July 2024, people born outside Illinois can change the sex designation on an Illinois birth certificate. Driver's licences and state identification are corrected on a Gender Designation Change Form, with an X option available from 2024.

Single-occupancy public restrooms were designated gender-neutral by legislation passed 109-5 in the House and 53-0 in the Senate, signed in July 2019 and effective 1 January 2020. Chicago's Human Rights Ordinance, as amended in 2016, provides that each person determines their own gender identity, with no proof required beyond expression for bathroom access, and all Chicago public schools have had all-gender bathrooms by signage since December 2021. A May 2023 bill permitting use of multi-occupancy facilities consistent with a person's gender identity passed both chambers but had not been signed or vetoed.

Marriage equality was enacted by statute signed by Governor Pat Quinn on 20 November 2013 and effective 1 June 2014, after House approval 61-54 and Senate approval 32-21, superseding a 1996 statutory ban. Gender-neutral marriage certificates have been available under a July 2021 law, and 2023 legislation repealing out-of-jurisdiction null-and-void provisions took effect in 2024. Civil unions have been recognised since 1 June 2011 under a law signed on 31 January 2011, with out-of-state marriages of same-sex couples recognised as civil unions. The Illinois Domestic Violence Act is written in gender-neutral terms and applies to partners who share or have shared a dwelling or a dating relationship.

Private consensual same-sex sexual activity has been lawful since 1 January 1962, when a new criminal code eliminated the state's sodomy law, making Illinois the first state to do so. The age of consent is 17, raised from 16 effective 1 January 2012.
tangentialFactors:
Illinois law does not govern federal documents, entry screening or federal facilities. Passports, visas and airport screening are set nationally, so the state's protections do not alter what a trans visitor encounters at a port of entry or in federal custody.

Des Plaines repealed its opposite-sex clothing ban in July 2021, the last such local ordinance recorded in the sources.

The 1983 HIV infection public health law was repealed by a May 2021 bill effective on the governor's signature.

Lurie Children's Hospital in Chicago apologised in July 2020 for past non-consensual infant surgeries performed to make genitalia appear more typically male or female, and announced it would stop such procedures unless medically necessary.
localsOnly:
Illinois Medicaid covers reassignment surgery costs for applicants aged 21 and over. In June 2024 the Department of Human Services and the Public Health Institute of Metropolitan Chicago announced an expansion of services through the Transgender and Gender Diverse Wellness and Equity Program.

Amending an Illinois birth certificate for a person born in the state requires an Affidavit and Certificate of Correction Request, a Declaration of Gender Transition or Intersex Condition completed by a licensed health or mental health professional, and a $15 fee.

Bullying based on gender identity or expression is prohibited, with requirements for school investigation, protection of student privacy and staff training. A 30 June 2019 executive order established a task force and procedures covering names, pronouns and dress codes for transgender students.

Funeral and burial instructions may specify gender identity and preferred pronouns under HB 3552, passed 79-34 in the House and 49-0 in the Senate, signed on 20 August 2015 and effective 1 January 2016.

Adoption by gay individuals or partners, including second-parent adoptions, is permitted, with access to IVF and gestational surrogacy.
outOfScopeNotes:
The May 2023 bill permitting use of multi-occupancy facilities consistent with gender identity passed both chambers; whether it was signed or vetoed is not resolved in the sources.

Whether Illinois's shield law withstands out-of-state subpoenas or civil actions directed at providers is not sourced.

The July 2026 ranking is a rubric-based assessment of tracked legislation rather than a measure of enforcement or outcomes on the ground.

Hate-crime reporting and prosecution data for gender-identity-motivated offences in Illinois are not sourced.

Implementation of the July 2024 provision allowing people born outside Illinois to amend an Illinois birth certificate is not documented in the sources.
